items.caption:
Asleep, your nose is a poor alarm. Your ears aren't.
In a small 2004 Brown University lab study (6 young adults), peppermint got no response in deeper sleep and harsh pyridine only some, while a tone got a response on at least 75% of trials. Smoke itself wasn't tested.

Expected: higher watched-full % and average watch time than the control.
items.caption:
Some brains make better earplugs.
In a 2010 lab study of 12 volunteers, those who made more sleep spindles on a quiet night were harder to rouse with noise on later noisy nights. The thalamus may act as a sound gate. Still a hypothesis.
